blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: Diffraction and interference phenomena occupy a prominent place in the phenomenology of quantum physics, Young's double-slit experiment (DSE) being an archetypal example which, according to Feynman "has in it the heart of quantum mechanics" [@Feynman]. Quantum physicists have discussed the DSE and augments thereof, e.g., the which-way [@Zurek; @WWM], or the delayed-choice DSE [@Wheeler], with varying degrees of rigour. Bohmian mechanics (also called the de Broglie-Bohm theory or pilot-wave theory) is a theory describing point particles moving along trajectories that grounds the formalism and predictions of standard quantum mechanics [@BohmHiley; @HollandBook; @DurrTeufel; @DGZOperators]. blocks.title: Concluding remarks
blocks.content:
The computation of the probability distribution of ToFs of quantum particles is one of the last
areas where experts disagree about what quantum mechanics should predict. While a cornucopia
of different ToF distributions exists in the literature, one rarely finds a discussion of the joint
distribution of impact positions and ToFs studied in this work. In this paper, we have considered a
Bohmian approach to this problem.
